subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep only per-job `payload.toolsAllow`?
rationale: This changes the security boundary and public config surface for scheduled agents, and automation cannot choose the permanent operator-facing policy or upgrade semantics safely.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the canonical scheduled-agent policy with documented precedence over broad config and interaction with per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron runs like subagent envelopes for tool-policy purposes, reducing config surface but coupling two distinct execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Decline a new global cron policy and document `payload.toolsAllow` / `openclaw cron --tools` as the supported hard restriction path.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the canonical scheduled-agent policy with documented precedence over broad config and interaction with per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior detailed review and is the strongest available routing signal for the current cron/config policy boundary.
